# 2. Training Data — Load and Inspect

```{r load-data}
raw_data <- read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE, na = c("", "NA", "N/A", "NULL", "null"))

# Make column names consistent and R-friendly.
raw_data <- raw_data %>% clean_names()
```


# 3. Training Data — Cleaning

## 3.1 Yes/No to Binary Conversion

```{r yes no conversion}
yes_no_cols <- raw_data %>%
  select(where(is.character)) %>%
  select(where(~ all(na.omit(.) %in% c("Yes", "No")))) %>%
  names()


raw_data <- raw_data %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(yes_no_cols), ~ ifelse(. == "Yes", 1, 0)))
```

## 3.2 Categorical Variables to Factors

```{r factor-conversion}
# Convert ID to character
raw_data$customer_id <- as.character(raw_data$customer_id)

# Convert all character columns to factor
raw_data <- raw_data %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))

# Make ordinal ones ordered
raw_data <- raw_data %>%
  mutate(
    income_group  = factor(income_group,  ordered = TRUE),
    credit_rating = factor(credit_rating, ordered = TRUE)
  )

# Convert binary 0/1 variables to factor

binary_vars <- c(
  "handset_refurbished",
  "handset_web_capable",
  "has_credit_card",
  "owns_computer",
  "owns_motorcycle",
  "truck_owner",
  "rv_owner",
  "buys_via_mail_order",
  "responds_to_mail_offers",
  "opt_out_mailings",
  "children_in_hh",
  "made_call_to_retention_team"
)

raw_data <- raw_data %>%
  mutate(across(
    all_of(binary_vars),
    ~ factor(., levels = c(0, 1))
  ))

# Convert churn to factor
raw_data <- raw_data %>%
  mutate(churn = factor(churn, levels = c(0, 1)))

# Verify structure
str(raw_data)
```

## 3.3 Missing Values — Investigation

```{r missing-counts}
missing_summary <- raw_data %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "missing_count") %>%
  mutate(
    missing_percent = round(100 * missing_count / nrow(raw_data), 2)
  ) 

missing_summary %>%
  filter(missing_count > 0) %>%
  kable()

# ── Investigate missing value overlap ─────────────────────────────────────────

usage_missing_vars <- c(
  "monthly_revenue", "monthly_minutes", "total_recurring_charge",
  "overage_minutes", "roaming_calls"
)

# Are the 91 missing rows the same rows across all five variables?
usage_missing_rows <- raw_data %>%
  filter(if_any(all_of(usage_missing_vars), is.na))

nrow(usage_missing_rows)  # expect 91 if fully overlapping

# Confirm all five are missing on the same rows
usage_missing_rows %>%
  select(all_of(usage_missing_vars)) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~sum(is.na(.))))

# Same check for age
age_missing_rows <- raw_data %>%
  filter(is.na(age_hh1) | is.na(age_hh2))

nrow(age_missing_rows)  # expect 520

age_missing_rows %>%
  summarise(
    missing_hh1 = sum(is.na(age_hh1)),
    missing_hh2 = sum(is.na(age_hh2))
  )

# Do the two groups overlap?
overlap <- raw_data %>%
  filter(
    if_any(all_of(usage_missing_vars), is.na) &
    (is.na(age_hh1) | is.na(age_hh2))
  )

nrow(overlap)

# Profile the missing rows — do they share characteristics?
raw_data %>%
  mutate(usage_missing = if_any(all_of(usage_missing_vars), is.na)) %>%
  group_by(usage_missing) %>%
  summarise(
    churn_rate    = mean(churn == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_tenure    = mean(months_in_service, na.rm = TRUE),
    n             = n()
  )

raw_data %>%
  mutate(age_missing = as.integer(is.na(age_hh1))) %>%
  group_by(age_missing) %>%
  summarise(
    churn_rate = mean(churn == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_tenure  = mean(months_in_service, na.rm = TRUE),
    n           = n()
  )
```

## 3.6 Age Columns — Zero Values and Flags

```{r age-checks}
age_cols <- intersect(c("age_hh1", "age_hh2"), names(raw_data))

age_checks <- map_dfr(age_cols, function(col) {
  tibble(
    column = col,
    age_zero_count = sum(raw_data[[col]] == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    age_below_18_count = sum(raw_data[[col]] > 0 & raw_data[[col]] < 18, na.rm = TRUE),
    age_above_100_count = sum(raw_data[[col]] > 100, na.rm = TRUE),
  )
})

age_checks %>% kable()

age_zero_rows <- raw_data %>%
  filter(if_any(all_of(age_cols), ~ . == 0)) %>%
  nrow()
age_zero_rows %>% kable()

# Age flags and cleaning

raw_data <- raw_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Flag rows where BOTH ages are zero — household composition unknown
    age_unknown = as.integer(
      (is.na(age_hh1) | age_hh1 == 0) &
      (is.na(age_hh2) | age_hh2 == 0)
    ),

    # household_has_two_adults: only 1 where hh2 is valid and hh1 is also valid
    # If age_unknown = 1, we cannot confirm any adults — defaults to 0
    household_has_two_adults = as.integer(
      !is.na(age_hh2) & age_hh2 != 0 &
      !is.na(age_hh1) & age_hh1 != 0
    ),

    # Convert all zero ages to NA so median imputation handles them uniformly
    age_hh1 = ifelse(age_hh1 == 0, NA, age_hh1),
    age_hh2 = ifelse(age_hh2 == 0, NA, age_hh2)
  )

# Verify
table(raw_data$age_unknown, useNA = "ifany")
table(raw_data$household_has_two_adults, useNA = "ifany")

# Confirm the two flags are consistent
raw_data %>%
  count(age_unknown, household_has_two_adults)

raw_data %>%
  filter((is.na(age_hh1) | age_hh1 == 0) & (!is.na(age_hh2) & age_hh2 != 0)) %>%
  nrow() #there is no cases where age hh2 has a value and age hh1 = 0 --> age hh1 is the primary age variable

# Convert all flags to factors

flag_vars <- c(
  "household_has_two_adults",
  "age_unknown",
  "usage_data_imputed",
  "zero_revenue_active"
)

raw_data <- raw_data %>%
  mutate(across(
    all_of(flag_vars),
    ~ factor(., levels = c(0, 1))
  ))

# Verify
raw_data %>%
  select(all_of(flag_vars)) %>%
  str()
```

```{r}
set.seed(31)

train_index <- createDataPartition(raw_data$churn, p = 0.7, list = FALSE)
train_raw   <- raw_data[ train_index, ]
test_raw    <- raw_data[-train_index, ]

# Confirm churn balance preserved
prop.table(table(train_raw$churn))
prop.table(table(test_raw$churn))
```

# 5. Imputation (Training-Derived Statistics)
```{r imputation}

# ── Compute imputation statistics from training set only ──────────────────────

num_cols <- c(
  "monthly_revenue", "monthly_minutes", "total_recurring_charge",
  "overage_minutes", "roaming_calls", "current_equipment_days",
  "age_hh1", "handsets"
)

num_cols <- intersect(num_cols, names(train_raw))

train_medians <- train_raw %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(num_cols), ~ median(., na.rm = TRUE)))

train_mode_service <- train_raw$service_area %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  table() %>%
  sort(decreasing = TRUE) %>%
  names() %>%
  .[1]

# Display numeric imputation values (medians) used from training set
train_medians_display <- train_medians %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "median_imputed_value")

print(train_medians_display)

# Display categorical imputation value (mode) for service_area
cat("Mode imputed for service_area:", train_mode_service, "\n")

impute_df <- function(df, medians, mode_sa) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      total_recurring_charge = ifelse(
        total_recurring_charge < 0, NA, total_recurring_charge
      ),
      across(
        all_of(names(medians)),
        ~ ifelse(is.na(.), medians[[cur_column()]], .)
      ),
      # Convert to character first to avoid factor integer coercion
      service_area = as.character(service_area),
      service_area = ifelse(is.na(service_area), mode_sa, service_area),
      service_area = as.factor(service_area)
    )
}

train_data <- impute_df(train_raw, train_medians, train_mode_service)
test_data  <- impute_df(test_raw,  train_medians, train_mode_service)

train_data$age_hh2 <-NULL
test_data$age_hh2 <- NULL
# Verify all — numeric and service_area
train_data %>%
  select(all_of(num_cols), service_area) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.))))

test_data %>%
  select(all_of(num_cols), service_area) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.))))
```

# 6. Feature Engineering
```{r}

# ── Feature engineering — applied to both sets via function ───────────────────

engineer_features <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      # Call quality
      total_call_issues = dropped_calls + blocked_calls + unanswered_calls,
      call_issue_rate   = ifelse(
        monthly_minutes > 0,
        total_call_issues / monthly_minutes,
        NA_real_
      ),

      # Usage efficiency
      revenue_per_minute = ifelse(
        monthly_minutes > 0,
        monthly_revenue / monthly_minutes,
        NA_real_
      ),
      overage_rate = ifelse(
        monthly_minutes > 0,
        overage_minutes / monthly_minutes,
        NA_real_
      ),

      # Equipment
      equipment_age_relative_to_tenure = ifelse(
        months_in_service > 0,
        current_equipment_days / (months_in_service * 30),
        NA_real_
      ),

      # Tenure and usage groupings (EDA reference only)
      tenure_group = cut(
        months_in_service,
        breaks        = c(0, 12, 24, 36, Inf),
        labels        = c("0-12", "13-24", "25-36", "36+"),
        include.lowest = TRUE
      ),
      usage_level = factor(
        case_when(
          monthly_minutes < 300 ~ "Low",
          monthly_minutes < 800 ~ "Medium",
          TRUE                  ~ "High"
        ),
        levels  = c("Low", "Medium", "High"),
        ordered = TRUE
      ),

      # Service area decomposition
      service_area  = as.character(service_area),
      sa_market     = as.factor(substr(service_area, 1, 3)),
      sa_locality   = as.factor(substr(service_area, 4, 6)),
      sa_area_code  = as.factor(substr(service_area, 7, 9))
    )
}

train_data <- engineer_features(train_data)
test_data  <- engineer_features(test_data)

# Sanity check
glimpse(train_data)
glimpse(test_data)
```

```{r correlation-heatmaps}
# Function to plot heatmap
plot_corr <- function(vars, title) {
  vars <- intersect(vars, names(train_data))
  
  if (length(vars) > 1) {
    # Convert factors to numeric for correlation only
    cor_data <- train_data %>%
      select(all_of(vars)) %>%
      mutate(across(where(is.factor), ~ as.numeric(.) - 1))
    
    cor_mat <- cor(cor_data, use = "complete.obs")
    
    corrplot(
      cor_mat,
      method      = "color",
      type        = "upper",
      addCoef.col = "black",
      tl.cex      = 0.8,
      number.cex  = 0.7,
      title       = title,
      mar         = c(0, 0, 1, 0)
    )
  }
}

plot_corr(usage_vars,     "Usage Variables")
plot_corr(retention_vars, "Retention Variables")
plot_corr(revenue_vars,   "Revenue Variables")
plot_corr(engineered_vars,   "Engineered Variables")

# ── Clean display labels (snake_case -> Title Case) ─────────────────────────
clean_labels <- function(vars) {
  vars %>%
    str_replace_all("_", " ") %>%
    str_to_title()
}

# ── Function to build a correlation plot (ggcorrplot, report-styled) ────────
plot_corr <- function(vars, title) {
  vars <- intersect(vars, names(train_data))
  if (length(vars) < 2) return(NULL)

  cor_data <- train_data %>%
    select(all_of(vars)) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.factor), ~ as.numeric(.) - 1))

  cor_mat <- cor(cor_data, use = "complete.obs")
  colnames(cor_mat) <- rownames(cor_mat) <- clean_labels(colnames(cor_mat))

  ggcorrplot(
    cor_mat,
    type       = "upper",
    lab        = TRUE,
    lab_size   = 3,
    hc.order   = TRUE,             # hierarchical clustering: groups correlated vars together
    outline.col = "white",
    colors     = c("#1f3864", "white", "#c8860d"),  # navy - white - gold, matches report palette
    title      = title,
    ggtheme    = theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
  ) +
    theme(
      plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12, hjust = 0),
      axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
      axis.text.y     = element_text(size = 8),
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.title    = element_blank(),
      panel.grid      = element_blank()
    )
}

# ── Generate each panel ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
p_usage      <- plot_corr(usage_vars,      "Usage Variables")
p_retention  <- plot_corr(retention_vars,  "Retention Variables")
p_revenue    <- plot_corr(revenue_vars,    "Revenue Variables")
p_engineered <- plot_corr(engineered_vars, "Engineered Variables")
```

## 6.2 Log Transformation
```{r}
# ── Histogram matrix — all numeric variables ──────────────────────────────────

train_data %>%
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Numeric Variables",
       x = NULL, y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

# ── Log transformation — all numeric variables ────────────────────────────────

numeric_vars <- train_data %>%
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  names()

log_transform <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(across(
      all_of(numeric_vars),
      ~ log1p(.),
      .names = "log_{.col}"   
    ))
}

train_data <- log_transform(train_data)
test_data <- log_transform(test_data)

# Verify new columns created
train_data %>%
  select(starts_with("log_")) %>%
  names()

# Histogram matrix of log columns
train_data %>%
  select(starts_with("log_")) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "darkgreen", colour = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Distribution After Log Transformation",
       x = NULL, y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7))
```

# 7. Build Modelling Datasets

SA-market churn-rate binning and the model-ready `train_model` / `test_model` data frames used by every model in Section 10.
```{r}

set.seed(31)

# ── SA market binning — computed from training set only ───────────────────────

market_rates <- train_data %>%
  group_by(sa_market) %>%
  summarise(
    churn_rate = mean(as.numeric(as.character(churn)), na.rm = TRUE),
    n          = n(),
    .groups    = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n >= 30)

# Check spread
summary(market_rates$churn_rate)

# Tertile breaks — guarantees all 3 levels
tertile_breaks <- quantile(market_rates$churn_rate, probs = c(0, 1/3, 2/3, 1))
cat("Tertile breaks:", tertile_breaks, "\n")

market_bins <- market_rates %>%
  mutate(
    sa_market_group = case_when(
      churn_rate >= tertile_breaks[3] ~ "High",
      churn_rate >= tertile_breaks[2] ~ "Medium",
      TRUE                            ~ "Low"
    ),
    sa_market_group = factor(sa_market_group, levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High"))
  ) %>%
  select(sa_market, sa_market_group)

# Verify all three levels present
table(market_bins$sa_market_group)

# ── 2. Build modelling datasets — all variables except explicitly excluded ─────

exclude_vars <- c(
  # Geography — replaced by sa_market_group
  "sa_market",
  "sa_locality",
  "sa_area_code",
  "service_area",

  # EDA only groupings
  "tenure_group",
  "usage_level",

  # Identifier/Not useful flags
  "customer_id",
  "usage_data_imputed",
  "zero_revenue_active",
  "household_has_two_adults",
  
  #Multicollinearity
  "total_call_issues",
  "log_total_call_issues",

  # Raw numeric variables — replaced by log_ versions for LR
  "months_in_service",
  "equipment_age_relative_to_tenure",
  "retention_calls",
  "retention_offers_accepted",
  "inbound_calls",
  "outbound_calls",
  "call_waiting_calls",
  "total_call_issues",
  "monthly_revenue",
  "monthly_minutes",
  "total_recurring_charge",
  "age_hh1",
  "overage_minutes",
  "roaming_calls",
  "current_equipment_days",
  "handsets",
  "dropped_calls",
  "blocked_calls",
  "unanswered_calls",
  "customer_care_calls",
  "threeway_calls",
  "call_forwarding_calls",
  "active_subs",
  "call_issue_rate",
  "overage_rate",
  "revenue_per_minute"
)

prepare_model_data <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    left_join(market_bins, by = "sa_market") %>%
    mutate(churn = factor(
      ifelse(churn == "Yes" | churn == 1, "Yes", "No"),
      levels = c("No", "Yes")
    )) %>%
    select(-all_of(exclude_vars)) %>%
    drop_na() %>%
    droplevels()
}

train_model <- prepare_model_data(train_data)
test_model  <- prepare_model_data(test_data)

# Confirm variables going into model
cat("Variables in model:\n")
print(setdiff(names(train_model), "churn"))

cat("\nDimensions — train:", dim(train_model), "\n")
cat("Dimensions — test: ", dim(test_model),  "\n")
prop.table(table(train_model$churn))

# No CV control
ctrl_none <- trainControl(method = "none", classProbs = TRUE)
```


# 8. Evaluation Data — Load, Clean, and Prepare

## 8.1 Load the Evaluation Data

```{r load-eval}
eval_path <- "eval_data.csv"
eval_raw <- read_csv(eval_path, show_col_types = FALSE,
                      na = c("", "NA", "N/A", "NULL", "null"))

eval_raw <- eval_raw %>% clean_names()

dim(eval_raw)
str(eval_raw)
```

## 8.2 Structure and Summary

```{r summary-eval}
summary(eval_raw)
```

## 8.3 Duplicate Checks

```{r duplicates-eval}
eval_raw %>% get_dupes() %>% nrow()

eval_raw %>%
  count(customer_id) %>%
  filter(n > 1)
```

## 8.4 Yes/No Conversion

```{r yes-no-eval}
yes_no_cols_eval <- setdiff(yes_no_cols, "churn")
eval_raw <- eval_raw %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(yes_no_cols_eval), ~ ifelse(. == "Yes", 1, 0)))
```

## 8.5 Categorical Variables to Factors

```{r factor-conversion-eval}
eval_raw$customer_id <- as.character(eval_raw$customer_id)

eval_raw <- eval_raw %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))

eval_raw <- eval_raw %>%
  mutate(
    income_group  = factor(income_group,  ordered = TRUE),
    credit_rating = factor(credit_rating, ordered = TRUE)
  )

eval_raw <- eval_raw %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(binary_vars), ~ factor(., levels = c(0, 1))))

str(eval_raw)
```

```{r check-unseen-levels}
# Reuses raw_data (training, already cleaned/factored above) — no need to
# re-read training_data.csv from disk a second time.

cat_cols_to_check <- c("occupation", "marital_status", "prizm_code", "service_area")

unseen_levels <- map_dfr(cat_cols_to_check, function(col) {
  train_levels <- unique(na.omit(as.character(raw_data[[col]])))
  eval_levels  <- unique(na.omit(as.character(eval_raw[[col]])))
  new_levels   <- setdiff(eval_levels, train_levels)
  tibble(
    column      = col,
    n_new_levels = length(new_levels),
    new_levels   = paste(head(new_levels, 10), collapse = ", ")
  )
})

print(unseen_levels)
cat("\nIf n_new_levels > 0 anywhere above, resolve before modelling.\n")
```

## 8.6 Missing Values and Usage-Block Flag

```{r missing-counts-eval}
missing_summary_eval <- eval_raw %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "missing_count") %>%
  mutate(missing_percent = round(100 * missing_count / nrow(eval_raw), 2))

missing_summary_eval %>% filter(missing_count > 0) %>% kable()
```

```{r}
usage_missing_vars <- c(
  "monthly_revenue", "monthly_minutes", "total_recurring_charge",
  "overage_minutes", "roaming_calls", "age_hh1", "age_hh2"
)

eval_raw <- eval_raw %>%
  mutate(
    usage_data_imputed = as.integer(
      is.na(monthly_revenue) &
      is.na(monthly_minutes) &
      is.na(total_recurring_charge) &
      is.na(overage_minutes) &
      is.na(roaming_calls)
    )
  )

table(eval_raw$usage_data_imputed, useNA = "ifany")
```

## 8.7 Invalid and Suspicious Data Checks

```{r negative-values-eval}
non_negative_cols <- eval_raw %>%
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  names()

eval_raw %>%
  filter(if_any(all_of(non_negative_cols), ~ . < 0))

eval_raw <- eval_raw %>%
  mutate(
    total_recurring_charge = ifelse(total_recurring_charge < 0, NA, total_recurring_charge),
    monthly_revenue = ifelse(monthly_revenue < 0, NA, monthly_revenue)
  )
```

```{r inconsistent-checks-eval}
eval_raw %>% filter(active_subs > 0 & months_in_service == 0)

eval_raw %>% filter(active_subs > 0 & monthly_revenue == 0)

eval_raw <- eval_raw %>%
  mutate(
    zero_revenue_active = as.integer(active_subs > 0 & monthly_revenue == 0)
  )

eval_raw %>% filter(handsets == 0 & current_equipment_days > 0)
```

## 8.8 Age Columns — Zero Values and Flags

```{r age-checks-eval}
age_cols <- intersect(c("age_hh1", "age_hh2"), names(eval_raw))

age_checks_eval <- map_dfr(age_cols, function(col) {
  tibble(
    column = col,
    age_zero_count = sum(eval_raw[[col]] == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    age_below_18_count = sum(eval_raw[[col]] > 0 & eval_raw[[col]] < 18, na.rm = TRUE),
    age_above_100_count = sum(eval_raw[[col]] > 100, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
})

age_checks_eval %>% kable()

age_zero_rows_eval <- eval_raw %>%
  filter(if_any(all_of(age_cols), ~ . == 0)) %>%
  nrow()
age_zero_rows_eval %>% kable()

eval_raw <- eval_raw %>%
  mutate(
    age_unknown = as.integer(
      (is.na(age_hh1) | age_hh1 == 0) &
      (is.na(age_hh2) | age_hh2 == 0)
  ))
#No age data is 0, no need ton convert to NA
#No age data is 0, no need for household_has_two_adults flag (flag is also not used in modelling)

table(eval_raw$age_unknown, useNA = "ifany")

flag_vars <- c("age_unknown","zero_revenue_active", "usage_data_imputed")

eval_raw <- eval_raw %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(flag_vars), ~ factor(., levels = c(0, 1))))
```

```{r feature-engineering-eval}
# Reuses engineer_features() from the training section above — this also

eval_data <- engineer_features(eval_data)

glimpse(eval_data)
```

```{r log-transform-eval}
eval_data %>% select(starts_with("log_")) %>% names()
```

## 8.12 SA Market Group (Churn-Rate Tertile Bins from Training)

```{r sa-market-group-eval}
# Reuses `market_bins`, already built in the training "Modelling" section
# above (filter(n >= 30), tertile breaks computed from train_data). Do NOT
# recompute market_rates/tertile_breaks/market_bins here.

eval_data <- eval_data %>%
  left_join(market_bins, by = "sa_market")

n_unmapped <- sum(is.na(eval_data$sa_market_group))
cat("Eval customers with an sa_market not seen in training (n >= 30 rule):", n_unmapped, "\n")

eval_data <- eval_data %>%
  mutate(sa_market_group = fct_na_value_to_level(sa_market_group, level = "Medium"))

table(eval_data$sa_market_group, useNA = "ifany")
```

## 8.13 Build the Model-Ready Evaluation Dataset (eval_model)

```{r prepare-eval-model}
# This mirrors training's exclude_vars, with one deliberate difference:
# "household_has_two_adults" is NOT included here, because eval_data never
# computes that flag. tenure_group and usage_level ARE included here now
# that engineer_features() is reused from training and creates them on
# eval_data too.

exclude_vars <- c(
  # Geography — replaced by sa_market_group
  "sa_market",
  "sa_locality",
  "sa_area_code",
  "service_area",

  # EDA only groupings
  "tenure_group",
  "usage_level",

  # Identifier/Not useful flags
  "customer_id",
  "usage_data_imputed",
  "zero_revenue_active",

  #Multicollinearity
  "total_call_issues",
  "log_total_call_issues",

  # Raw numeric variables — replaced by log_ versions for LR
  "months_in_service",
  "equipment_age_relative_to_tenure",
  "retention_calls",
  "retention_offers_accepted",
  "inbound_calls",
  "outbound_calls",
  "call_waiting_calls",
  "total_call_issues",
  "monthly_revenue",
  "monthly_minutes",
  "total_recurring_charge",
  "age_hh1",
  "overage_minutes",
  "roaming_calls",
  "current_equipment_days",
  "handsets",
  "dropped_calls",
  "blocked_calls",
  "unanswered_calls",
  "customer_care_calls",
  "threeway_calls",
  "call_forwarding_calls",
  "active_subs",
  "call_issue_rate",
  "overage_rate",
  "revenue_per_minute"
)

# Keep customer_id aside — needed later to build selected_customers_<zID>.csv
eval_customer_id <- eval_data$customer_id

eval_model <- eval_data %>%
  select(-all_of(exclude_vars)) %>%
  droplevels()

sum(eval_data$monthly_minutes == 0)

eval_model <- eval_data %>%
  mutate(
    log_call_issue_rate   = ifelse(is.na(log_call_issue_rate),   0, log_call_issue_rate),
    log_revenue_per_minute = ifelse(is.na(log_revenue_per_minute), 0, log_revenue_per_minute),
    log_overage_rate       = ifelse(is.na(log_overage_rate),       0, log_overage_rate)
  )

cat("Rows going into prediction:", nrow(eval_model), "(should be 10,000)\n")
cat("Any remaining NA cells by column:\n")
eval_model %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "n_na") %>%
  filter(n_na > 0) %>%
  print()

cat("\nVariables going into eval_model:\n")
print(names(eval_model))
```

```{r}
factor_cols <- eval_model %>% select(where(is.factor)) %>% names()

eval_model <- eval_model %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(factor_cols), ~ factor(as.character(.), levels = levels(train_model[[cur_column()]]))))

# Check how many NAs this introduces (i.e. how many genuinely unseen values existed)
eval_model %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(factor_cols), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything()) %>%
  filter(value > 0)
```

```{r eda-churn-distribution}
eda_data <- train_data

eda_data %>%
  count(churn) %>%
  mutate(
    pct   = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2),
    label = paste0(ifelse(churn == 1, "Churn", "No Churn"), 
                   "\n", n, " (", pct, "%)")
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = "", y = n, fill = factor(churn))) +
  geom_col(width = 1, colour = "white") +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("0" = "#003087", "1" = "#CC8800"),
    labels = c("0" = "No Churn", "1" = "Churn")
  ) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            colour   = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 4) +
  labs(title = "Churn Distribution", fill = NULL) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title   = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```

```{r professional visualization for report}
    y     = "Churn Rate (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title  = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title  = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.text   = element_text(size = 7),
    strip.text  = element_text(size = 8)
  )

# ── Combine side by side ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

p1 + plot_spacer() + p2 +
  plot_layout(widths = c(2, 0.15,2)) +
  plot_annotation(
    theme = theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA))
  )
#----------------

# ── Plot 1: Churn Rate by Tenure Group ───────────────────────────────────────

p3 <- eda_data %>%
  mutate(churn_num = as.numeric(churn == 1 | churn == "Yes")) %>%
  group_by(tenure_group) %>%
  summarise(churn_rate = mean(churn_num) * 100, .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = tenure_group, y = churn_rate, fill = tenure_group)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(churn_rate, 1)), vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "0-12"  = "#003087",
      "13-24" = "#CC8800",
      "25-36" = "#003087",
      "36+"   = "#003087"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Churn Rate by Tenure Group",
    x     = "Months in Service",
    y     = "Churn Rate (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title      = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title      = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.text       = element_text(size = 8)
  )

# ── Plot 2: Top and Bottom 10 Markets by Churn Rate ───────────────────────────

sa_market_churn <- eda_data %>%
  mutate(churn_num = as.numeric(churn == 1 | churn == "Yes")) %>%
  group_by(sa_market) %>%
  summarise(churn_rate = mean(churn_num) * 100, n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n >= 50) %>%
  arrange(desc(churn_rate))

p4 <- bind_rows(
  slice_head(sa_market_churn, n = 10),
  slice_tail(sa_market_churn, n = 10)
) %>%
  mutate(group = rep(c("Highest Churn", "Lowest Churn"), each = 10)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(reorder(sa_market, churn_rate), churn_rate, fill = group)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Highest Churn" = "#CC8800", "Lowest Churn" = "#003087"),
    name   = NULL
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Top and Bottom 10 Markets by Churn Rate",
    x     = "Market",
    y     = "Churn Rate (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title      = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title      = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.text       = element_text(size = 7)
  )

# ── Combine side by side ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

p3 + plot_spacer() + p4 +
  plot_layout(widths = c(2, 0.15, 2))
```

# 10. Predictive Modelling

## ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
## MODEL 1: LOGISTIC REGRESSION
## ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

```{r logistic-regression}
# ── MODEL 1: LOGISTIC REGRESSION ─────────────────────────────────────────────

set.seed(31)

# Use glm() directly — more memory efficient than caret for large variable sets
lr_model <- glm(
  churn ~ .,
  data   = train_model,
  family = binomial()
)

# ── Coefficient summary ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
lr_summary <- summary(lr_model)
print(lr_summary)

# Significant predictors only
lr_coefs <- as.data.frame(coef(lr_summary)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("variable") %>%
  rename(
    estimate  = Estimate,
    std_error = `Std. Error`,
    z_value   = `z value`,
    p_value   = `Pr(>|z|)`
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    significance = case_when(
      p_value < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p_value < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p_value < 0.05  ~ "*",
      p_value < 0.1   ~ ".",
      TRUE            ~ ""
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(p_value)

cat("\n── Significant predictors (p < 0.05) ──\n")
lr_coefs %>% filter(p_value < 0.05) %>% kable() %>% print() 

# ── Predictions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
lr_probs <- predict(lr_model, newdata = test_model, type = "response")
lr_preds <- factor(ifelse(lr_probs >= 0.5, "Yes", "No"),
                   levels = c("No", "Yes"))

confusionMatrix(lr_preds, test_model$churn, positive = "Yes")

# ── ROC and PR ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
lr_roc <- roc(test_model$churn, lr_probs, levels = c("No", "Yes"), quiet = TRUE)

# Check levels of both
levels(lr_preds)
levels(test_model$churn)

# Check what values are actually in test_model$churn
table(test_model$churn)

# Check lr_probs range
summary(lr_probs)

lr_pr <- pr.curve(
  scores.class0 = lr_probs[test_model$churn == "Yes"],
  scores.class1 = lr_probs[test_model$churn == "No"],
  curve         = TRUE
)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

plot(lr_roc,
     main = paste0("ROC Curve — Logistic Regression\nAUC = ", round(auc(lr_roc), 3)),
     col  = "steelblue", lwd = 2)

plot(lr_pr,
     main     = paste0("PR Curve — Logistic Regression\nAUC = ", round(lr_pr$auc.integral, 3)),
     col      = "steelblue", lwd = 2,
     auc.main = FALSE)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

cat("ROC AUC — Logistic Regression:", round(auc(lr_roc), 4), "\n")
cat("PR AUC  — Logistic Regression:", round(lr_pr$auc.integral, 4), "\n")
```

# ── MODEL 1B: LOGISTIC REGRESSION — SIGNIFICANT VARIABLES ONLY ───────────────
```{r}
set.seed(31)

# Extract significant base variable names (p < 0.05) from full model
# Strip factor level suffixes to get original column names
sig_vars <- lr_coefs %>%
  filter(p_value < 0.05, variable != "(Intercept)") %>%
  pull(variable)

# Match back to actual column names in train_model
# Factor variables appear as e.g. "occupationProfessional" — strip suffix
all_cols <- names(train_model %>% select(-churn))

sig_cols <- unique(unlist(lapply(all_cols, function(col) {
  if (any(startsWith(sig_vars, col))) col else NULL
})))

cat("Significant predictors selected:\n")
print(sig_cols)

# Build reduced datasets
train_lr_sig <- train_model %>% select(all_of(sig_cols), churn)
test_lr_sig  <- test_model  %>% select(all_of(sig_cols), churn)

# Fit reduced model
lr_model_sig <- glm(
  churn ~ .,
  data   = train_lr_sig,
  family = binomial()
)

summary(lr_model_sig)

# ── Predictions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
lr_probs_sig <- predict(lr_model_sig, newdata = test_lr_sig, type = "response")
lr_preds_sig <- factor(ifelse(lr_probs_sig >= 0.5, "Yes", "No"),
                       levels = c("No", "Yes"))

confusionMatrix(lr_preds_sig, test_lr_sig$churn, positive = "Yes")

# ── ROC and PR ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
lr_roc_sig <- roc(test_lr_sig$churn, lr_probs_sig,
                  levels = c("No", "Yes"), quiet = TRUE)

lr_pr_sig <- pr.curve(
  scores.class0 = lr_probs_sig[test_lr_sig$churn == "Yes"],
  scores.class1 = lr_probs_sig[test_lr_sig$churn == "No"],
  curve         = TRUE
)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

plot(lr_roc_sig,
     main = paste0("ROC Curve — LR Significant Only\nAUC = ",
                   round(auc(lr_roc_sig), 3)),
     col  = "steelblue", lwd = 2)

plot(lr_pr_sig,
     main     = paste0("PR Curve — LR Significant Only\nAUC = ",
                       round(lr_pr_sig$auc.integral, 3)),
     col      = "steelblue", lwd = 2,
     auc.main = FALSE)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

cat("ROC AUC — LR Significant Only:", round(auc(lr_roc_sig), 4), "\n")
cat("PR AUC  — LR Significant Only:", round(lr_pr_sig$auc.integral, 4), "\n")

# ── Comparison table — all variables vs significant only ─────────────────────

# Helper to extract confusion matrix metrics
get_cm_metrics <- function(preds, truth) {
  cm <- confusionMatrix(preds, truth, positive = "Yes")
  tibble(
    Precision   = round(cm$byClass["Precision"],   4),
    Recall      = round(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"], 4),
    F1          = round(cm$byClass["F1"],           4),
    Specificity = round(cm$byClass["Specificity"],  4),
    Accuracy    = round(cm$overall["Accuracy"],     4)
  )
}

lr_all_metrics <- get_cm_metrics(lr_preds,     test_model$churn)
lr_sig_metrics <- get_cm_metrics(lr_preds_sig, test_lr_sig$churn)

comparison_lr <- bind_rows(
  tibble(Model = "LR — All Variables",         
         ROC_AUC = round(auc(lr_roc),     4),
         PR_AUC  = round(lr_pr$auc.integral, 4)) %>%
    bind_cols(lr_all_metrics),
  
  tibble(Model = "LR — Significant Only",      
         ROC_AUC = round(auc(lr_roc_sig), 4),
         PR_AUC  = round(lr_pr_sig$auc.integral, 4)) %>%
    bind_cols(lr_sig_metrics)
)

cat("\n── Logistic Regression Comparison ──\n")
print(comparison_lr)
```

## MODEL 2: RANDOM FOREST
## ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

```{r random-forest}
set.seed(31)

mtry_fixed    <- floor(sqrt(ncol(train_model) - 1))
rf_grid_fixed <- expand.grid(mtry = mtry_fixed)

rf_model <- train(
  churn ~ .,
  data      = train_model,
  method    = "rf",
  trControl = ctrl_none,
  tuneGrid  = rf_grid_fixed,
  ntree     = 500
)

# ── Feature importance ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
rf_importance <- varImp(rf_model, scale = TRUE)
plot(rf_importance, top = 20, main = "Feature Importance — Random Forest")

# ── Predictions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
rf_probs <- predict(rf_model, test_model, type = "prob")[, "Yes"]
rf_preds <- predict(rf_model, test_model)

confusionMatrix(rf_preds, test_model$churn, positive = "Yes")

# ── ROC and PR ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
rf_roc <- roc(test_model$churn, rf_probs, levels = c("No", "Yes"), quiet = TRUE)

rf_pr <- pr.curve(
  scores.class0 = rf_probs[test_model$churn == "Yes"],
  scores.class1 = rf_probs[test_model$churn == "No"],
  curve         = TRUE
)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

plot(rf_roc,
     main = paste0("ROC Curve — Random Forest\nAUC = ", round(auc(rf_roc), 3)),
     col  = "#003087", lwd = 2)

plot(rf_pr,
     main     = paste0("PR Curve — Random Forest\nAUC = ", round(rf_pr$auc.integral, 3)),
     col      = "#CC8800", lwd = 2,
     auc.main = FALSE)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

cat("ROC AUC — Random Forest:", round(auc(rf_roc), 4), "\n")
cat("PR AUC  — Random Forest:", round(rf_pr$auc.integral, 4), "\n")
```

```{r}
# ── Cumulative Gains and Decile-Wise Chart — Random Forest (Boruta) ───────────

# ── 1. Build gains table ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

gains_table <- test_rf_boruta %>%
  mutate(prob = rf_probs_boruta) %>%
  arrange(desc(prob)) %>%
  mutate(
    rank          = row_number(),
    decile        = ntile(desc(prob), 10),
    actual_churn  = as.numeric(churn == "Yes"),
    cumulative_n  = row_number(),
    cumulative_churners = cumsum(actual_churn)
  ) %>%
  group_by(decile) %>%
  summarise(
    n                   = n(),
    churners            = sum(actual_churn),
    churn_rate          = mean(actual_churn) * 100,
    cumulative_n        = max(cumulative_n),
    cumulative_churners = max(cumulative_churners),
    .groups             = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    cumulative_pct_customers = cumulative_n / nrow(test_rf_boruta) * 100,
    cumulative_pct_churners  = cumulative_churners / sum(churners) * 100,
    lift                     = (churners / n) / (sum(churners) / nrow(test_rf_boruta))
  )
```

```{r}
# ── MODEL 3: XGBOOST ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


set.seed(31)

# ── Helper: build DMatrix from model dataframe ────────────────────────────────

# ── Helper: prepare XGBoost matrix without model.matrix ──────────────────────

prepare_xgb_matrix <- function(df, label_col = "churn") {
  labels <- as.numeric(df[[label_col]] == "Yes")
  
  # Remove label column
  df_features <- df %>% select(-all_of(label_col))
  
  # Convert each column type explicitly
  df_numeric <- df_features %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.factor), ~ as.numeric(.))) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.logical), ~ as.numeric(.))) %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), ~ as.numeric(.)))
  
  # Check for any remaining non-numeric
  cat("Non-numeric columns remaining:", 
      sum(!sapply(df_numeric, is.numeric)), "\n")
  cat("Dimensions:", dim(df_numeric), "\n")
  
  mat <- as.matrix(df_numeric)
  xgb.DMatrix(data = mat, label = labels)
}

dtrain <- prepare_xgb_matrix(train_model)
dtest  <- prepare_xgb_matrix(test_model)

# ── XGBoost parameters ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

xgb_params <- list(
  objective        = "binary:logistic",
  eval_metric      = "auc",
  eta              = 0.1,
  max_depth        = 6,
  min_child_weight = 1,
  subsample        = 0.8,
  colsample_bytree = 0.8
)

# ── Helper: evaluate model ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

evaluate_xgb <- function(model, dtest_mat, test_df, label) {
  probs <- predict(model, dtest_mat)
  preds <- factor(ifelse(probs >= 0.5, "Yes", "No"), levels = c("No", "Yes"))

  cat("\n══", label, "══\n")
  print(confusionMatrix(preds, test_df$churn, positive = "Yes"))

  roc_obj <- roc(test_df$churn, probs, levels = c("No", "Yes"), quiet = TRUE)
  pr_obj  <- pr.curve(
    scores.class0 = probs[test_df$churn == "Yes"],
    scores.class1 = probs[test_df$churn == "No"],
    curve         = TRUE
  )

  par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
  plot(roc_obj,
       main = paste0("ROC — ", label, "\nAUC = ", round(auc(roc_obj), 3)),
       col  = "firebrick", lwd = 2)
  plot(pr_obj,
       main     = paste0("PR — ", label, "\nAUC = ", round(pr_obj$auc.integral, 3)),
       col      = "firebrick", lwd = 2,
       auc.main = FALSE)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

  cat("ROC AUC:", round(auc(roc_obj), 4), "\n")
  cat("PR AUC: ", round(pr_obj$auc.integral, 4), "\n")

  list(model = model, probs = probs, roc = roc_obj, pr = pr_obj)
}

## ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
## XGBOOST — ALL VARIABLES
## ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

xgb_model <- xgb.train(
  params        = xgb_params,
  data          = dtrain,
  nrounds       = 200,
  watchlist     = list(train = dtrain, test = dtest),
  verbose       = 1,
  print_every_n = 20
)

# Feature importance
xgb_importance <- xgb.importance(
  feature_names = names(train_model %>% 
                          select(-churn) %>%
                          mutate(across(where(is.factor), as.numeric))),
  model = xgb_model
)
xgb.plot.importance(xgb_importance, top_n = 20,
                    main = "Feature Importance — XGBoost All Variables")

# Evaluate
xgb_results <- evaluate_xgb(xgb_model, dtest, test_model, "XGBoost — All Variables")
```

```{r model-comparison}
# ── 0. Helper function ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

get_all_metrics <- function(probs, true_labels, model_name, threshold = 0.5) {
  preds <- factor(ifelse(probs >= threshold, "Yes", "No"),
                  levels = c("No", "Yes"))
  cm <- confusionMatrix(preds, true_labels, positive = "Yes")
  tibble(
    Model       = model_name,
    Accuracy    = round(cm$overall["Accuracy"],    4),
    Kappa       = round(cm$overall["Kappa"],       4),
    Sensitivity = round(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"], 4),
    Precision   = round(cm$byClass["Precision"],   4),
    F1          = round(cm$byClass["F1"],          4)
  )
}
```

# ── Threshold Tuning — LR and RF (Boruta) ────────────────────────────────────
```{r}
thresholds <- seq(0.1, 0.9, by = 0.01)

# ── 1. Threshold tuning function ──────────────────────────────────────────────

tune_threshold <- function(probs, true_labels, model_name) {
  map_dfr(thresholds, function(t) {
    preds <- factor(ifelse(probs >= t, "Yes", "No"),
                    levels = c("No", "Yes"))
    cm <- confusionMatrix(preds, true_labels, positive = "Yes")
    tibble(
      model       = model_name,
      threshold   = t,
      sensitivity = cm$byClass["Sensitivity"],
      precision   = cm$byClass["Precision"],
      specificity = cm$byClass["Specificity"],
      f1          = cm$byClass["F1"]
    )
  })
}

lr_thresholds <- tune_threshold(lr_probs, test_model$churn, "Logistic Regression")
rf_thresholds <- tune_threshold(rf_probs_boruta, test_rf_boruta$churn, "Random Forest")

all_thresholds <- bind_rows(lr_thresholds, rf_thresholds)

# ── 2. Plot threshold curves ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

all_thresholds %>%
  pivot_longer(cols     = c(sensitivity, precision, f1),
               names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  ggplot(aes(threshold, value, colour = metric)) +
  geom_line(lwd = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5,  linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~ model) +
  labs(title = "Threshold Tuning — LR and RF (Boruta)",
       x = "Threshold", y = "Value") +
  theme_minimal()

# ── 3. Find optimal thresholds ────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Youden's J optimised — pROC::coords()
roc_lr <- roc(test_model$churn, lr_probs, levels = c("No", "Yes"), direction = "<")
roc_rf <- roc(test_rf_boruta$churn, rf_probs_boruta, levels = c("No", "Yes"), direction = "<")

youden_lr <- coords(roc_lr, "best", best.method = "youden",
                     ret = c("threshold", "sensitivity", "specificity"))
youden_rf <- coords(roc_rf, "best", best.method = "youden",
                     ret = c("threshold", "sensitivity", "specificity"))

best_youden <- bind_rows(
  tibble(model = "Logistic Regression", threshold = youden_lr$threshold,
         sensitivity = youden_lr$sensitivity, specificity = youden_lr$specificity),
  tibble(model = "Random Forest", threshold = youden_rf$threshold,
         sensitivity = youden_rf$sensitivity, specificity = youden_rf$specificity)
)

# F1 optimised
best_f1 <- all_thresholds %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  filter(f1 == max(f1, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  select(model, threshold, sensitivity, precision, f1)

cat("\n── Best threshold by Youden's J ──\n")
print(best_youden)

cat("\n── Best threshold by F1 ──\n")
print(best_f1)

# ── 4. Evaluate all three thresholds per model ────────────────────────────────

evaluate_threshold <- function(probs, true_labels, model_name, t, label) {
  preds <- factor(ifelse(probs >= t, "Yes", "No"),
                  levels = c("No", "Yes"))
  cm <- confusionMatrix(preds, true_labels, positive = "Yes")
  tibble(
    Model       = model_name,
    Threshold   = paste0(label, " (", round(t, 3), ")"),
    Sensitivity = round(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"], 4),
    Precision   = round(cm$byClass["Precision"],   4),
    F1          = round(cm$byClass["F1"],           4),
    Specificity = round(cm$byClass["Specificity"],  4),
    Accuracy    = round(cm$overall["Accuracy"],     4)
  )
}

# LR thresholds
t_lr_youden <- best_youden %>% filter(model == "Logistic Regression") %>% pull(threshold)
t_lr_f1     <- best_f1     %>% filter(model == "Logistic Regression") %>% pull(threshold)

# RF (Boruta) thresholds
t_rf_youden <- best_youden %>% filter(model == "Random Forest") %>% pull(threshold)
t_rf_f1     <- best_f1     %>% filter(model == "Random Forest") %>% pull(threshold)

comparison_threshold <- bind_rows(
  # Logistic Regression
  evaluate_threshold(lr_probs, test_model$churn, "Logistic Regression", 0.50,        "Default"),
  evaluate_threshold(lr_probs, test_model$churn, "Logistic Regression", t_lr_youden, "Youden's J"),
  evaluate_threshold(lr_probs, test_model$churn, "Logistic Regression", t_lr_f1,     "F1"),

  # Random Forest (Boruta)
  evaluate_threshold(rf_probs_boruta, test_rf_boruta$churn, "Random Forest", 0.50,        "Default"),
  evaluate_threshold(rf_probs_boruta, test_rf_boruta$churn, "Random Forest", t_rf_youden, "Youden's J"),
  evaluate_threshold(rf_probs_boruta, test_rf_boruta$churn, "Random Forest", t_rf_f1,     "F1")
)

cat("\n── Threshold Comparison — LR and RF (Boruta) ──\n")
print(comparison_threshold)

# ── 5. Visual summary ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

comparison_threshold %>%
  pivot_longer(cols     = c(Sensitivity, Precision, F1, Specificity),
               names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Value") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Threshold, y = Value, fill = Metric)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~ Model) +
  labs(title = "Performance by Threshold Strategy — LR and RF (Boruta)",
       x = "Threshold Strategy", y = "Value") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))

# ── Confusion Matrix — Best Model (RF Boruta) at Best Threshold (F1-optimised) ──

final_preds <- factor(ifelse(rf_probs_boruta >= t_rf_f1, "Yes", "No"),
                       levels = c("No", "Yes"))

final_cm <- confusionMatrix(final_preds, test_rf_boruta$churn, positive = "Yes")

cat("\n── Final Confusion Matrix — Random Forest (Boruta) @ Threshold", round(t_rf_f1, 3), "──\n")
print(final_cm)

# report

comparison_threshold %>%
  mutate(across(c(Sensitivity, Precision, F1, Specificity, Accuracy),
                ~ round(., 3))) %>%
  kable(
    caption = "Model Performance by Threshold Strategy",
    align   = c("l", "l", "c", "c", "c", "c", "c")
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
    full_width        = FALSE,
    position          = "center"
  ) %>%

    which(comparison_threshold$Model == "Random Forest" &

  )
#--
final_preds <- factor(ifelse(rf_probs_boruta >= t_rf_f1, "Yes", "No"),
                      levels = c("No", "Yes"))

final_cm <- confusionMatrix(final_preds, test_rf_boruta$churn, positive = "Yes")
cm_table <- as.data.frame(final_cm$table) %>%

# Pivot to wide for display

# ── Lock in the final selected model ──────────────────────────────────────────
# RF (Boruta) is now the model carried forward into the persona breakdown,
# evaluation scoring, and decision optimisation sections below. Saving it
# here guarantees identical downstream results (predictions, SHAP/break-down
# values, thresholds) regardless of how many times this script is re-knit or
```

# 11. Persona Break-Down Analysis

```{r}
# ── Persona Break-Down Analysis — RF Boruta Variables ─────────────────────────

set.seed(31)

# ── 1. Create explainer ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

explainer_rf <- explain(
  model   = rf_model_boruta,
  data    = test_rf_boruta %>% select(-churn),
  y       = as.numeric(test_rf_boruta$churn == "Yes"),
  label   = "Random Forest (Boruta)",
  verbose = FALSE
)

# ── 2. Select three personas ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

test_with_probs <- test_rf_boruta %>% mutate(prob = rf_probs_boruta)

# Persona 1 — High risk: top 10% predicted probability
persona_churn <- test_with_probs %>%
  filter(prob >= quantile(prob, 0.90)) %>%
  mutate(dist = abs(prob - median(prob[prob >= quantile(prob, 0.90)]))) %>%
  arrange(dist) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  select(-churn, -prob, -dist)

prob_churn <- test_with_probs %>%
  filter(prob >= quantile(prob, 0.90)) %>%
  pull(prob) %>% median()

# Persona 2 — Low risk: bottom 10% predicted probability
persona_stays <- test_with_probs %>%
  filter(prob <= quantile(prob, 0.10)) %>%
  mutate(dist = abs(prob - median(prob[prob <= quantile(prob, 0.10)]))) %>%
  arrange(dist) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  select(-churn, -prob, -dist)

prob_stays <- test_with_probs %>%
  filter(prob <= quantile(prob, 0.10)) %>%
  pull(prob) %>% median()

# Persona 3 — Borderline: closest to threshold
persona_border <- test_with_probs %>%
  mutate(dist = abs(prob - t_rf_f1)) %>%
  arrange(dist) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  select(-churn, -prob, -dist)

prob_border <- test_with_probs %>%
  mutate(dist = abs(prob - t_rf_f1)) %>%
  arrange(dist) %>%
  pull(prob) %>% first()

cat("Persona 1 — High Risk (top 10%):", round(prob_churn,  4), "\n")
cat("Persona 2 — Low Risk (bottom 10%):", round(prob_stays,  4), "\n")
cat("Persona 3 — Borderline:", round(prob_border, 4), "\n")

# ── 3. Compute break-down ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

bd_churn  <- predict_parts(explainer_rf, persona_churn,  type = "break_down")
bd_stays  <- predict_parts(explainer_rf, persona_stays,  type = "break_down")
bd_border <- predict_parts(explainer_rf, persona_border, type = "break_down")

# ── 4. Un-log personas for readable display ───────────────────────────────────

log_cols_present <- names(persona_churn) %>% keep(~ startsWith(., "log_"))
raw_counterparts <- str_remove(log_cols_present, "^log_")

unlog_persona <- function(persona_df) {
  persona_df %>%
    select(-any_of(raw_counterparts)) %>%
    mutate(across(all_of(log_cols_present), ~ expm1(.))) %>%
    rename_with(~ str_remove(., "^log_"), all_of(log_cols_present))
}

persona_churn_unlog  <- unlog_persona(persona_churn)
persona_stays_unlog  <- unlog_persona(persona_stays)
persona_border_unlog <- unlog_persona(persona_border)

# ── 5. Custom waterfall plot with un-logged values ────────────────────────────

plot_waterfall <- function(bd_obj, unlogged_persona, title, predicted_prob) {
  unlogged_df <- as.data.frame(unlogged_persona)

  bd_df <- as.data.frame(bd_obj) %>%
    filter(!variable_name %in% c("intercept", "")) %>%
    filter(!grepl("prediction|intercept", variable)) %>%
    slice_head(n = 10) %>%
    arrange(contribution)

  display_labels <- vector("character", nrow(bd_df))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(bd_df))) {
    v_clean <- str_remove(bd_df$variable_name[i], "^log_")
    if (!is.na(v_clean) && v_clean %in% names(unlogged_df)) {
      val <- round(as.numeric(unlogged_df[[v_clean]]), 2)
      display_labels[i] <- paste0(v_clean, " = ", val)
    } else {
      display_labels[i] <- as.character(bd_df$variable_value[i])
    }
  }

  bd_df <- bd_df %>%
    mutate(
      display_value = display_labels,
      direction     = ifelse(contribution > 0, "Increases Risk", "Decreases Risk")
    )

  # Dynamically extend x-axis to fit labels
  x_max <- max(bd_df$contribution, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.35
  x_min <- min(bd_df$contribution, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.35

  bd_df %>%
    ggplot(aes(reorder(display_value, contribution), contribution,
               fill = direction)) +
    geom_col() +
    geom_text(aes(
      label = round(contribution, 3),
      hjust = ifelse(contribution >= 0, -0.15, 1.15)
    ), size = 3) +
    coord_flip(clip = "off") +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(min(x_min, -0.005), x_max),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.2))
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(
      "Increases Risk" = "#d73027",
      "Decreases Risk" = "#4575b4"
    )) +
    labs(
      title    = title,
      subtitle = paste0("Predicted churn probability: ", round(predicted_prob, 3)),
      x        = NULL,
      y        = "Contribution to predicted probability",
      fill     = NULL
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle   = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 9)
    )
}

# ── 6. Plot all three personas ────────────────────────────────────────────────

print(plot_waterfall(bd_churn,  persona_churn_unlog,
                     "Persona 1: Typical Churner",     prob_churn))

print(plot_waterfall(bd_stays,  persona_stays_unlog,
                     "Persona 2: Typical Non-Churner", prob_stays))

print(plot_waterfall(bd_border, persona_border_unlog,
                     "Persona 3: Borderline",          prob_border))

# Check all factor level mappings ─────────────────────────────────────────────

train_data %>%
  summarise(across(
    c(call_issue_rate, monthly_minutes, active_subs, current_equipment_days, monthly_revenue, inbound_calls, outbound_calls, equipment_age_relative_to_tenure, dropped_calls, overage_minutes, age_hh1, overage_rate),
    list(
      min    = ~ min(., na.rm = TRUE),
      median = ~ median(., na.rm = TRUE),
      max    = ~ max(., na.rm = TRUE),
      mean   = ~ round(mean(., na.rm = TRUE), 2)
    )
  )) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to  = c("variable", "stat"),
               names_sep = "_(?=[^_]+$)") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = stat, values_from = value)
```

# 12. Evaluation Scoring, Decision Optimisation and Stochastic Risk Analysis

## 12.1 Discount-Offer Threshold Optimisation
```{r}
# Step 1: Predicted churn probability + annual revenue for each eval customer.

eval_probs <- predict(rf_model_boruta, eval_model, type = "prob")[, "Yes"]
max(eval_probs)

cat("nrow(eval_model):", nrow(eval_model), "\n")
cat("length(eval_probs):", length(eval_probs), "\n")

stopifnot(length(eval_probs) == nrow(eval_data))

eval_R <- 12 * eval_data$monthly_revenue   # predicted annual revenue R_i
stopifnot(length(eval_R) == length(eval_probs)) 

# Step 2: Algebraic break-even threshold (derived above).
breakeven_threshold <- 0.05 / 0.14
cat("Algebraic break-even threshold:", round(breakeven_threshold, 4), "\n")

# Step 3: Expected profit under each action, as functions of p and R.
expected_profit_no_offer <- function(p, R) (1 - p) * 0.15 * R
expected_profit_offer    <- function(p, R) (1 - 0.1 * p) * 0.10 * R

# Step 4: Sweep thresholds 0→1. At each t, offer to customers with p_i >= t;
# sum total portfolio profit under that rule.
thresholds_seq <- seq(0, 1, by = 0.001)

profit_sensitivity <- map_dfr(thresholds_seq, function(t) {
  offer_flag <- eval_probs >= t
  total_profit <- sum(ifelse(
    offer_flag,
    expected_profit_offer(eval_probs, eval_R),
    expected_profit_no_offer(eval_probs, eval_R)
  ))
  tibble(threshold = t, n_offered = sum(offer_flag), total_profit = total_profit)
})

# Baseline = profit if NO customer is offered anything (t = Inf, effectively).
baseline_profit <- sum(expected_profit_no_offer(eval_probs, eval_R))

profit_sensitivity <- profit_sensitivity %>%
  mutate(profit_uplift = total_profit - baseline_profit)

# Step 5: Find the empirically profit-maximising threshold.
optimal_row <- profit_sensitivity %>%
  filter(total_profit == max(total_profit)) %>%
  slice(1)

cat("Empirically optimal threshold:", optimal_row$threshold, "\n")
cat("Customers offered at optimum:", optimal_row$n_offered, "\n")
cat("Profit uplift vs. no action:", round(optimal_row$profit_uplift, 2), "\n")

# Step 6: Sensitivity chart — required deliverable for this section.
ggplot(profit_sensitivity, aes(x = threshold, y = profit_uplift)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#003087", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = breakeven_threshold,
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "#CC8800", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = optimal_row$threshold,
             linetype = "dotted", colour = "#003087", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text",
           x     = breakeven_threshold + 0.01,
           y     = max(profit_sensitivity$profit_uplift) * 0.95,
           label = paste0("Break-even\n", round(breakeven_threshold, 3)),
           colour = "#CC8800", size = 3, hjust = 0) +
  annotate("text",
           x     = optimal_row$threshold + 0.01,
           y     = max(profit_sensitivity$profit_uplift) * 0.85,
           label = paste0("Optimum\n", optimal_row$threshold),
           colour = "#003087", size = 3, hjust = 0) +
  labs(
    title    = "Portfolio Profit Uplift by Discount-Offer Threshold (RF Boruta)",
    subtitle = paste0("Break-even = ", round(breakeven_threshold, 3),
                      " | Empirical optimum = ", optimal_row$threshold),
    x        = "Churn probability threshold (offer if p ≥ threshold)",
    y        = "Expected profit uplift vs. no action ($)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 9, colour = "grey50"),
    axis.title    = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.text     = element_text(size = 8)
  )

# Step 7: Check whether the 3,000-customer operational cap binds.

n_at_breakeven <- sum(eval_probs >= breakeven_threshold)
cat("Customers exceeding break-even threshold:", n_at_breakeven, "\n")

# ── Trade-off visualization: cumulative profit by number of customers contacted ──

# Step 1: Rank all 10,000 eval customers by per-customer profit uplift, descending.
uplift_per_customer <- expected_profit_offer(eval_probs, eval_R) -
                        expected_profit_no_offer(eval_probs, eval_R)

ranked_customers <- tibble(
  rank   = seq_along(eval_probs),
  uplift = sort(uplift_per_customer, decreasing = TRUE)
) %>%
  mutate(cumulative_uplift = cumsum(uplift))

# Step 2: Identify the two reference points for the chart.
n_operational_cap <- 3000
n_profit_maximizing <- which.max(ranked_customers$cumulative_uplift)

profit_at_cap    <- ranked_customers$cumulative_uplift[n_operational_cap]
profit_at_optimum <- ranked_customers$cumulative_uplift[n_profit_maximizing]

cat("Profit-maximising n:", n_profit_maximizing,
    "| Cumulative uplift:", round(profit_at_optimum, 2), "\n")
cat("At operational cap (n=3000) | Cumulative uplift:", round(profit_at_cap, 2), "\n")
cat("Profit foregone by capping at 3,000:", round(profit_at_optimum - profit_at_cap, 2), "\n")

# Step 3: Plot.
ggplot(ranked_customers, aes(x = rank, y = cumulative_uplift)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue", lwd = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = n_operational_cap, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = n_profit_maximizing, linetype = "dotted", colour = "darkgreen") +
  annotate("text", x = n_operational_cap, y = min(ranked_customers$cumulative_uplift),
           label = paste0("Operational cap\n(n=", n_operational_cap, ")"),
           colour = "firebrick", vjust = 0, hjust = -0.05, size = 3.2) +
  annotate("text", x = n_profit_maximizing, y = max(ranked_customers$cumulative_uplift),
           label = paste0("Profit-maximising\n(n=", n_profit_maximizing, ")"),
           colour = "darkgreen", vjust = 1, hjust = 1.05, size = 3.2) +
  labs(
    title = "Cumulative Profit Uplift vs. Number of Customers Contacted (RF Boruta)",
    subtitle = "Customers ranked by individual profit uplift, highest first",
    x = "Number of customers contacted (ranked by profit uplift)",
    y = "Cumulative expected profit uplift ($)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 12.2 Evaluation Selection and Submission (Top 3,000 by Predicted Risk)

```{r}
# Step 1: Identify the 3,000 highest-risk customers
top3000 <- tibble(
  customer_id = eval_customer_id,
  p           = eval_probs,
  R           = eval_R
) %>%
  arrange(desc(p)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 3000)

# Step 2: Apply your final decision threshold (break-even = 0.05/0.14) to
# determine which of these 3,000 customers actually receive the discount
# offer under your recommended rule. 
breakeven_threshold <- 0.05 / 0.14

top3000 <- top3000 %>%
  mutate(
    offered = p >= breakeven_threshold,
    # Effective churn probability under the chosen action:
    # offer -> churn prob multiplied by 0.1 (90% reduction, per the brief)
    # no offer -> churn prob unchanged
    p_effective = ifelse(offered, p * 0.1, p),
    # Profit if the customer stays, under the chosen action
    profit_if_stays = ifelse(offered, 0.10 * R, 0.15 * R)
  )

cat("Customers offered discount in this population:", sum(top3000$offered), "\n")
cat("Customers not offered (below break-even):", sum(!top3000$offered), "\n")

# ── Write submission CSV ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

top3000 %>%
  select(customer_id) %>%
  write_csv("selected_customers_z5516343.csv")

cat("CSV written with", nrow(top3000), "customers\n")
```

## 12.3 Stochastic Risk Analysis — Monte Carlo Simulation

Monte Carlo simulation on the top 3,000 highest-risk eval customers (scored by RF Boruta), under the recommended retention-action rule from Section 12.1.

```{r}
set.seed(31)

n_customers <- nrow(top3000)
p_vec <- top3000$p_effective
R_vec <- top3000$R
profit_stay_vec <- top3000$profit_if_stays

# ── Convergence check: run at increasing simulation sizes to confirm the
# estimates stabilise, and report the number of runs used to justify it ────
convergence_check <- function(nsim) {
  set.seed(31)
  churn_draws <- matrix(
    rbinom(nsim * n_customers, size = 1, prob = rep(p_vec, each = nsim)),
    nrow = nsim, ncol = n_customers
  )
  total_churns <- rowSums(churn_draws)
  # Profit per sim: 0 if churned, profit_if_stays otherwise
  profit_matrix <- sweep(1 - churn_draws, 2, profit_stay_vec, `*`)
  total_profit <- rowSums(profit_matrix)

  tibble(
    nsim = nsim,
    p95_churns = quantile(total_churns, 0.95),
    p5_profit  = quantile(total_profit, 0.05)
  )
}

convergence_results <- map_dfr(c(100, 250, 500, 2000, 5000, 10000, 20000), convergence_check)
convergence_results %>% kable() %>% print()

n_sim <- 10000

# ── Final simulation at chosen n_sim ─────────────────────────────────────────
set.seed(31)
churn_draws <- matrix(
  rbinom(n_sim * n_customers, size = 1, prob = rep(p_vec, each = n_sim)),
  nrow = n_sim, ncol = n_customers
)

total_churns_sim <- rowSums(churn_draws)
profit_matrix    <- sweep(1 - churn_draws, 2, profit_stay_vec, `*`)
total_profit_sim <- rowSums(profit_matrix)

# ── Required outputs ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
p95_total_churns <- quantile(total_churns_sim, 0.95)
p5_total_profit  <- quantile(total_profit_sim, 0.05)

cat("\n══ Stochastic Risk Analysis Results (n_sim =", n_sim, ") ══\n")
cat("Mean total churns across simulations:", round(mean(total_churns_sim), 1), "\n")
cat("95th percentile (1-in-20 worst-case) total churns:", round(p95_total_churns, 0), "\n")
cat("Mean total profit across simulations: $", round(mean(total_profit_sim), 2), "\n")
cat("5th percentile (1-in-20 worst-case) total profit: $", round(p5_total_profit, 2), "\n")

# ── Visualisation — distribution of both metrics with the percentile marked ──
p5 <- ggplot(tibble(x = total_churns_sim), aes(x)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "#CC8800", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = p95_total_churns, colour = "firebrick", linetype = "dashed", lwd = 1) +
  labs(title = "Simulated Total Churns — Top 3,000 Highest-Risk Customers",
       subtitle = paste0("95th percentile (1-in-20 worst case) = ", round(p95_total_churns, 0)),
       x = "Total churns", y = "Simulation count") +
  theme_minimal()

p6 <- ggplot(tibble(x = total_profit_sim), aes(x)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "#003087", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = p5_total_profit, colour = "firebrick", linetype = "dashed", lwd = 1) +
  labs(title = "Simulated Total Profit — Top 3,000 Highest-Risk Customers",
       subtitle = paste0("5th percentile (1-in-20 worst case) = $", round(p5_total_profit, 0)),
       x = "Total profit ($)", y = "Simulation count") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p5)
print(p6)

running_convergence <- tibble(
  n = seq(100, n_sim, by = 150),
  running_p95 = map_dbl(seq(100, n_sim, by = 150), ~ quantile(total_churns_sim[1:.x], 0.95))
)

ggplot(running_convergence, aes(x = n, y = running_p95)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Convergence of 95th-Percentile Churn Estimate",
       x = "Number of simulation runs", y = "Running 95th percentile (total churns)") +
  theme_minimal()


# Standard error of a quantile estimate via bootstrap — a direct,
# defensible way to answer "how many runs do I need"
percentile_se <- function(x, prob, n_boot = 500) {
  boot_estimates <- replicate(n_boot, quantile(sample(x, replace = TRUE), prob))
  sd(boot_estimates)
}

se_p95_churns <- percentile_se(total_churns_sim, 0.95)
se_p5_profit  <- percentile_se(total_profit_sim, 0.05)

cat("SE of 95th percentile churns:", round(se_p95_churns, 2), "\n")
cat("SE of 5th percentile profit: $", round(se_p5_profit, 2), "\n")
```
